items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The only actual playing that I ever did with Duke Ellington was a radio show... Duke beckoned to me from the audience... to come up, and pointed to the bass. So I did. I went up, picked up the bass... So we started.

ctx.x: Yes. Was there a moment when in this environment Duke Ellington came to dinner at a house or at . . .?

That’s after – my wife and I lived with my aunt. My aunt had a friend, a very close friend, and she lived with us. Her daughter was married to Duke Ellington. Whenever he came to town, he’d always come to the house and have dinner. I met him long before I got involved musically, but I got to know him from him coming to my aunt’s house to have dinner. I met him for the first time that way. Then later on, when I moved to New York and got to know him – had been around the band and seen him at broadcasts and all that…
Let’s get to 52nd Street. But in Chicago, as you were beginning to play, can you talk about that, before you went to 52nd Street, the early . . .?
